With three lines (mug-1, lamp-1, pen-1), the loop sums only the first two: 2×12.50 + 39.99 = 64.99, silently skipping the pens line (3×1.00 = 3.00). Expected 67.99. The off-by-one exactly reproduces the report ($67.99 − $64.99 = $3.00 = the last line). It would also return 0.00 for a single-item cart. The rest of subtotal() (to_money rounding, LineItem.total bulk discount) is correct per README rules. The defect is the loop bound; it must iterate over every line item.

payload.root_cause: Cart.subtotal() in pyshop/cart.py uses `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)`, an off-by-one loop that iterates over all line items except the last one. For a cart with lines [2×mug ($25.00), 1×lamp ($39.99), 3×pen ($3.00)], it sums only the first two lines: 25.00 + 39.99 = 64.99, dropping the last line's $3.00, hence the reported subtotal of $64.99 instead of $67.99. The loop should visit every item (e.g., `for item in self.items: total += item.total`).

Reported values match exactly: expected 2×12.50 + 39.99 + 3×1.00 = 67.99; buggy result 25.00 + 39.99 = 64.99 (difference $3.00 equals the skipped pens line).
tests/test_cart.py:21-25 (test_subtotal_sums_all_lines) asserts the correct 67.99 for this exact scenario, confirming the intended behavior.
pyshop/cart.py:34-43 — Cart.add() appends each distinct SKU as a separate LineItem, so pens is the third (last) item and is the one skipped.
